name: Hoabinhian
title: The story of the Hoabinhian people

text: Thousands of years ago, the Hoabinhian people hunted and gathered across Southeast Asia, from Vietnam and Thailand to Malaysia.
They often lived in rock shelters by streams and ate shellfish, fish, snails, nuts, fruit and small animals.
src: The Hoabinhian is a tradition of stone tools, chiefly flaked river cobbles, left by hunter-gatherers across mainland Southeast Asia / more than 120 sites in Vietnam / Spirit Cave, Sai Yok, Tham Lod and Ban Rai in Thailand / Gua Cha in Malaysia

oriented towards rock shelters near freshwater streams in upland limestone country / living species of shellfish, fish, and small to medium-sized mammals / limestone mountains gave land snails and small mammals / the valley floors gave nuts, fruits

text: They made tools by chipping big river stones, often on one side only.
The oldest of these tools, found in a rock shelter in Yunnan in China, are more than 40,000 years old.
src: flaked cobble tools, often worked on one face only / a mainly one-sided flaking tradition on water-rounded pebbles
in 2016 a rock shelter at Xiaodong in Yunnan, China, produced Hoabinhian artefacts dating from 41,500 BCE / Xiaodong in Yunnan, China, the oldest

text: The Hoabinhian is named after Hòa Bình in Vietnam, where Madeleine Colani dug up its tools nearly 100 years ago.
In 1994 archaeologists, people who dig up the past, met in the city of Hanoi and agreed to keep the name.
src: It was first defined from Madeleine Colani’s excavations in Hòa Bình province, northern Vietnam / 1927: Madeleine Colani publishes her nine excavations in the northern Vietnamese province of Hòa Bình
1994: A conference in Hanoi votes to keep the term

text: Later, farmers came into Southeast Asia from southern China and mixed with the hunters.
Today peoples such as the Maniq and the Semang share family roots with them, as their DNA shows.
src: Farming came with movements of people between southern China and Southeast Asia, with which the Neolithic there is associated / Neolithic samples from the mainland carry mostly East Asian-related ancestry like that of ancient southern China, with a smaller share of Hoabinhian-related ancestry
Ancient DNA from two Hoabinhian individuals shows a deeply branching East Asian ancestry, shared most closely today with peoples such as the Andamanese Onge and Jarawa, the Semang and the Maniq
